goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method == :raw_html, bypassing the sanitization pipeline and Plugin::Filter, and Jobs::PollFeed feeds unsanitized third-party RSS/Atom HTML into TopicEmbed.import which is rendered with raw post.cooked, causing stored XSS

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum and changes `Post#cook` to immediately `return raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and also skipping `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and sets `raw` to third-party HTML (`contents` from RSS/Atom via `Jobs::PollFeed` using `i.content.scrub` and `CGI.unescapeHTML`, and via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` using `Readability::Document#content`). None of these paths sanitize the HTML before storing it, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`; for `:raw_html`, `post.cooked == post.raw`. This is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the diff (arbitrary script/event-handler HTML from feeds/remote pages can be persisted and served to clients).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb and topic_embed.rb use Kernel#open on a user-supplied URL, which executes a subprocess when the string begins with '|', allowing command injection
Feed fetching via open() has no timeout, redirect limit, or response-size cap, so a slow or huge feed hangs or OOMs the Sidekiq worker

adjudication.rationale: In the new scheduled job `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed is fetched with `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the remote page is fetched via `open(url).read`. In both cases, the diff shows no explicit networking safeguards (no open/read timeout options passed to `open`, no maximum response size enforcement, and no explicit redirect limiting). As written, a very large response can be read into memory during parsing/`read`, and a slow/blocked upstream can tie up the Sidekiq job while the request is in progress.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb uses setnx followed by a separate expire, which is not atomic; if the worker or Redis fails between calls the retrieved:<url> key never expires and the embed URL is throttled permanently

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then, in a separate call, `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic. If the process crashes, is killed, or Redis errors out after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key `retrieved:<embed_url>` will remain without a TTL. On subsequent calls, `setnx` will return false, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return true forever for that URL, effectively permanently throttling retrieval. This is a real correctness defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first followed by create! is a check-then-act race; concurrent jobs both create topics and the second create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, leaving an orphaned topic/post

adjudication.rationale:
Yes, there is a check-then-act race in `TopicEmbed.import`: it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` while the migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. Two concurrent jobs can both see no row and then the second insert will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`.

However, the finding’s specific claim about “leaving an orphaned topic/post” is not clearly supported by the diff because the create path is wrapped in `Topic.transaction do ... PostCreator.create ... TopicEmbed.create! ... end`; if `create!` raises, the transaction should roll back the post/topic created in that same transaction. The unhandled exception/race is real; the orphaned-record consequence is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) runs unconditionally even when revisor.revise! returns false, so the revision is lost permanently and later polls always see 'unchanged'

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed is found and the content_sha1 differs, the code calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. Since `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (e.g., if `should_revise?` is false due to permissions/locked post/other conditions) without raising, this can advance `content_sha1` even though the post was not updated. Future polls will then see matching SHA1s and skip updating, leaving the embedded post permanently stale for that content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.post can be nil when the post was deleted (no dependent: handling and no null guard), so PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError and kills the whole PollFeed run

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content changed, immediately does `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)` without guarding against `post` being `nil`. The association is `belongs_to :post` with no `dependent:` cleanup anywhere in this diff, and the migration only adds a `post_id` column (no FK constraint). If the referenced post is deleted (or the row is otherwise missing), `embed.post` will return `nil`, causing `PostRevisor.new(nil)` to blow up and abort the caller (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` which calls `TopicEmbed.import` in a loop). This is a concrete nil-dereference path present in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: An already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb is edited to add force: true, which issues DROP TABLE top_topics and destroys existing rows if the migration is re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which would destroy any existing `top_topics` rows if that migration is ever re-run (e.g., via redo/reset or in an environment where the table exists but the migration is executed again). This data-loss behavior is directly introduced by the change in the diff.

matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags the same underlying problem: `i.content` can be nil for many RSS 2.0 feeds (using description instead of content), causing `nil.scrub` to raise. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb tests for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' pass vacuously because feed_polling_enabled? remains false and short-circuits the guard

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute, poll_feed runs only if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the examples "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub `feed_polling_url` or `embed_by_username` respectively, but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Since the default in the added `config/site_settings.yml` is `feed_polling_enabled: false`, these specs can pass without ever exercising the missing-url/missing-username branches (short-circuit on `feed_polling_enabled?`). That makes the tests potentially vacuous with respect to what their descriptions claim to verify.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with '/' and strips all leading slashes, mangling protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.jpg and leaving genuinely relative paths like images/wat.jpg untouched

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are rewritten only when `href`/`src` `start_with?('/')`, and then it does `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` before prefixing: `"#{prefix}/#{...}"`. This will treat protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg` as if they were site-root relative and rewrite them to something like `http://<embed_host>/cdn.example.com/x.jpg`, which is incorrect. At the same time, genuinely relative URLs that don’t start with `/` (e.g. `images/wat.jpg` or `../img.png`) are not rewritten at all, despite the method’s stated goal of converting relative URLs to absolute. This is a verifiable correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: contents << "\n<hr>…" mutates the caller's string in place, appending the footer repeatedly on retry/reuse and raising FrozenError on frozen input

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the String object passed by the caller (in-place append). That side effect is directly verifiable in the diff. If the caller reuses the same `contents` object across multiple import attempts/calls, the footer will be appended repeatedly, changing `content_sha1` and the stored post body. Also, if a caller ever passes a frozen string, `<<` will raise FrozenError. While the current shown call sites likely pass fresh, mutable strings, the introduced method as written does have this concrete mutating-argument behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the --category option and silently repoints topic creation from PostCreator to TopicEmbed.import_remote, breaking existing -c invocations and adding an uncontrolled HTTP fetch per thread, undocumented in the PR description

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line and all `category_id` handling are removed, so existing invocations using `-c/--category` will now fail with an unknown option (a backward-incompatible CLI change). The import logic also changes from `PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](...)]" ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read`, meaning it will issue an HTTP fetch for each thread link (previously it did not fetch remote content). The claim about being "undocumented in the PR description" is not verifiable from the diff, but the behavioral changes above are directly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: discourse_expires_in 1.minute is applied to the loading render, so the loading page's 30-second self-reload is served from cache and the frame can stay on 'Loading Discussion…' past the point the topic exists

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after the `if topic_id ... else render 'loading'` branch. That means the loading response also gets a 1-minute cache lifetime. The loading template uses `document.location.reload()` after 30 seconds (without the `true` argument), which can reload from cache while the cached response is still fresh (30s < 60s). In that case, the iframe can repeatedly re-display the cached loading page even after the topic has been created, until the cache entry expires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parent.postMessage passes the full request.referer URL (including path/query) as targetOrigin, and an empty referer produces '' which makes postMessage throw a SyntaxError and break iframe resizing
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that postMessage is using the full referrer URL (including path/query) as targetOrigin, which is the same core problem as the golden comment (targetOrigin must be just the origin or messages will be dropped/break resizing). It also adds an extra related issue about empty referer causing a SyntaxError, but the underlying mismatch is the same.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The postMessage height call is inside window.onload, so the iframe height is sent exactly once and never updates as content loads

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the embedded page posts its height to the parent in `window.onload`. `onload` fires after the document and its dependent resources (including images like avatars/logo) have finished loading, so the computed `document['body'].offsetHeight` should reflect the fully loaded static server-rendered content (`embed/best.html.erb`). The diff does not introduce any client-side dynamic content changes inside the iframe after load that would require repeated resize messages. Therefore, claiming it “never updates as content loads” is not a verifiable defect from this diff; it’s speculative about future/dynamic resizing behavior not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js has no null check on document.getElementById('discourse-comments'), so comments.appendChild throws if the host page lacks that element

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is assigned `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and is used immediately via `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no guard. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and this will throw a runtime TypeError, breaking the embed script.

adjudication_records.issue_text: discourseUrl + "embed/best?…" silently produces a broken URL unless the host page includes a trailing slash, which is undocumented

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe URL is built via simple string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. If `discourseUrl` is configured as a typical base like `https://forum.example.com` (no trailing `/`), the result becomes `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is an invalid/broken URL. Nothing in this diff normalizes `discourseUrl` (e.g., ensuring a trailing slash) or uses a proper URL-join, so the embed script is fragile and can silently break depending on how the host page sets `discourseUrl`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post.user.small_avatar_url / post.user.username raise NoMethodError when the post's author has been deleted, taking down the whole embed render

adjudication.rationale: The embed view does call `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without a nil-check, but the diff does not show (or change) any behavior that would make `post.user` nil. In typical Discourse data model `posts.user_id` is required and a "deleted" user generally still has a User row (soft-deleted/anonymized), so `post.user` would still exist. The claim that deletion causes `NoMethodError` is not verifiable from this diff and is speculative about application behavior outside the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key computes a 'feed-modified:' cache key that is never read or written, so the intended conditional-GET/Last-Modified short-circuit is unimplemented dead code and every hourly run re-downloads the full feed

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, a method `feed_key` is introduced that builds a Redis-style cache key (`"feed-modified:..."`), but that method is never called anywhere in the diff, and there is no code that reads/writes this key or uses it to perform conditional HTTP requests. Separately, `poll_feed` always executes `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on each run, so there is no implemented short-circuit based on a stored last-modified/etag value in this change. While the reviewer’s mention of “intended conditional-GET/Last-Modified” is an inference, the core issue—unused/dead `feed_key` and no caching to avoid repeated full downloads—is directly verifiable in the diff.
